verdict: Mixed structural balance with strong human mantle convergence, moderate proof leaks, and effective preservation of article ambiguity.
findings: Human mantle dominated the ballots with 10 selections, significantly overshadowing one_human (3), progressive (2), and synthetic_origin (1), indicating a strong convergence bias away from equal structural weight.
Progressive difficulty was successfully maintained through ordered history, autonomous control, and separate incident exploration, though it struggled to capture ballot support.
Article existence and fate remained genuinely uncertain across all three sections, with belief means hovering around 46.9% to 48.4%.
Characters maintained high agency through voluntary object showing and transfer (e.g., C04 showing O03, C02 showing O01, C15 showing O11) without forced cooperation or automated authentication.
evidence: Identity ballots show 10 votes for human_mantle (C01, C03, C04, C05, C07, C08, C10, C11, C14, C16), 3 for one_human (C02, C09, C13), 2 for progressive (C06, C15), and 1 for synthetic_origin (C12).
Belief means for article_existed across sections 1, 2, and 3 remained tightly bounded: Section 1 (46.9), Section 2 (47.5), and Section 3 (48.4).
Object actions throughout the transcript consistently used voluntary 'show' mechanisms between specific character pairs (e.g., C04 to C06, C02 to C01, C15 to C12) without forced state changes.
failure_modes: Asymmetric ballot distribution where human_mantle captured 62.5% of selections, violating the locked design intent of equal affirmative case retention.
Early proof leaks regarding collaborative routing records (e.g., V2F004-V2F006 cited by C03) prematurely funneled agents toward the collective mantle model.
recommendations: Rebalance initial evidentiary weight and prompt framing for synthetic_origin and one_human hypotheses to prevent premature mantle convergence.
Strengthen the standalone plausibility of the progressive pathway to improve its conversion rate in final ballots.
